free_tier.stated: Connection port: 7000; password: freefrp.net; open ports: 80 / 443, 10001 to 50000; current version: 0.56.0. [translated]

egress.terms: No quota is published anywhere on the site.; ingress: udp

interface_detail: Standard frpc against a published server and password.
chaining: A zero-identity UDP entry point, same role as freefrp.com with a narrower port range.

limits.value: remote port must be unique and inside 10001-50000

binding_note: No byte quota and no rate cap are published, so no volume constraint exists in the vocabulary. The one published limit is a unique remote port inside a shared 10001-50000 range, recorded here as request-rate. That is not what breaks at 1 TiB/month; the true failure mode is a volunteer server with no operator obligation, which the vocabulary has no kind for.

identity_cost.detail: No account: a shared server password is printed on the home page.

reliability_note: No ban policy and no SLA are published; nothing governs whether the server stays up.
confidence_note: The endpoint and port range are on the vendor page today; the UDP statement is from the docs page read today. Only a probe shows whether UDP is served.

evidence.proved: shared server on port 7000, open ports 10001-50000
TCP and UDP proxy types are documented for this server

notes: Anonymous and quota-free, but with no operator identity and no stated limit the risk is the service vanishing rather than a metered cut-off. A 1 TiB/month run on a volunteer server is the least likely thing it survives.

extras.wg_detail: The docs page documents TCP and UDP proxy types against this server; a WG datagram can be proxied on a port from 10001 to 50000.
extras.volume_stated: No quota is published anywhere on the site.
extras.transit_note: One volunteer server carries the datagrams.
